### workspace snapshot --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace snapshot --json [--name WORKSPACE]... [--pr]

Print one JSON document with everything a UI polls: each project's workspaces (running
state, git facts, agent panes, open questions, pipeline entries), the repo-wide locks
and the dev environment, plus a cursor into the event log taken before anything is read.

Reads only; nothing is written. A source that can't answer (tmux, an agent daemon, git,
gh) is reported as unavailable, never as clean. Agent daemons are read in parallel,
1 second each; a running workspace without one is listed in daemons_unavailable.

        --json                       Print schema-versioned JSON (see docs/README.snapshot.md); required
        --name WORKSPACE             Only this workspace (repeatable); its project's locks and dev are still included
        --pr                         Also read each branch's pull request with `gh pr view` (adds git.pr; slower)
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace snapshot --json    # one document with every project and workspace, for a UI or script to poll
  workspace snapshot --json --name my-app    # only one workspace, when a script watches a single project
  workspace snapshot --json --name my-app --name my-app.worktree-fix-login    # two workspaces in one read
  workspace snapshot --json --pr    # also read each branch's pull request, when you need review state
  workspace snapshot --json | jq -r '.projects[].members[] | select(.running) | .workspace'    # list the running workspaces
--- stderr
--- end

--- end
